name: I/O-Conscious Volume Rendering
definition: A volume rendering technique that hides disk I/O delay associated with large-scale volume data set rendering by overlapping disk accesses with rendering computation, using a data-driven approach to exploit parallelism while minimizing synchronization.
summary: I/O-Conscious Volume Rendering minimizes rendering time by using a dedicated prefetch thread that mirrors ray casting traversal to fetch data blocks exactly when needed, hiding disk I/O latency.
